scenario.description: Global WAN: four cities plus a cloud VPC, 2,000 IoT/scanner devices. Focus: IPsec VPN, multi-area OSPF/BGP, route summarization.

media.rationale: Selected Cat6a (10GBASE-T) because the 90 m run is within the 100 m limit defined by IEEE 802.3an; Cat6a sustains 10 Gbps at this distance without active optics.

Selected an ISP Carrier Ethernet handoff protected by IPsec because the 5000.0 km multi-city path cannot be served by a direct single-mode run at acceptable cost. The carrier provides the L1 transport and the enterprise overlay provides confidentiality and route isolation across the public WAN.

vlans.name: IoT
vlans.rationale: VLAN 10 (IoT) carries Warehouse sensors on 10.20.0.0/21 with gateway 10.20.0.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

vlans.name: Scanners
vlans.rationale: VLAN 20 (Scanners) carries Handheld scanners on 10.20.8.0/23 with gateway 10.20.8.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

vlans.name: Corporate
vlans.rationale: VLAN 30 (Corporate) carries City office users on 10.20.10.0/24 with gateway 10.20.10.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

vlans.name: Management
vlans.rationale: VLAN 40 (Management) carries Infrastructure management on 10.20.11.0/25 with gateway 10.20.11.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: root (priority 4096).

vlans.name: Guest
vlans.rationale: VLAN 50 (Guest) carries Visitor access on 10.20.11.128/27 with gateway 10.20.11.129. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

routing.rationale: Selected multi-area OSPF inside the enterprise and eBGP at the cloud VPC boundary because the design includes a cloud VPC plus 4 remote site(s). eBGP provides routing-domain isolation and policy control, while OSPF areas contain internal topology changes and allow summarisation.

rationales.rationale: Selected Cat6a (10GBASE-T) because the 90 m run is within the 100 m limit defined by IEEE 802.3an; Cat6a sustains 10 Gbps at this distance without active optics.

rationales.choice: ISP Carrier Ethernet + IPsec VPN / N/A (service handoff)
rationales.rationale: Selected an ISP Carrier Ethernet handoff protected by IPsec because the 5000.0 km multi-city path cannot be served by a direct single-mode run at acceptable cost. The carrier provides the L1 transport and the enterprise overlay provides confidentiality and route isolation across the public WAN.

rationales.condition: largest-first allocation with CIDR boundary alignment
rationales.rationale: Allocated 5 subnets from 10.20.0.0/16 using largest-first VLSM. Address-space utilisation is 4.54% and host utilisation is 67.43%.
Allocated 10.20.0.0/21 to IoT: 2046 usable addresses, gateway 10.20.0.1, wildcard 0.0.7.255. Blocks are aligned and checked for overlap with all previously allocated subnets.
Allocated 10.20.8.0/23 to Scanners: 510 usable addresses, gateway 10.20.8.1, wildcard 0.0.1.255. Blocks are aligned and checked for overlap with all previously allocated subnets.
Allocated 10.20.10.0/24 to Corporate: 254 usable addresses, gateway 10.20.10.1, wildcard 0.0.0.255. Blocks are aligned and checked for overlap with all previously allocated subnets.
Allocated 10.20.11.0/25 to Management: 126 usable addresses, gateway 10.20.11.1, wildcard 0.0.0.127. Blocks are aligned and checked for overlap with all previously allocated subnets.
Allocated 10.20.11.128/27 to Guest: 30 usable addresses, gateway 10.20.11.129, wildcard 0.0.0.31. Blocks are aligned and checked for overlap with all previously allocated subnets.

Selected multi-area OSPF inside the enterprise and eBGP at the cloud VPC boundary because the design includes a cloud VPC plus 4 remote site(s). eBGP provides routing-domain isolation and policy control, while OSPF areas contain internal topology changes and allow summarisation.

rationales.condition: segmentation by function with explicit trunk policy
rationales.rationale: VLAN 10 (IoT) carries Warehouse sensors on 10.20.0.0/21 with gateway 10.20.0.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

rationales.condition: segmentation by function with explicit trunk policy
rationales.rationale: VLAN 20 (Scanners) carries Handheld scanners on 10.20.8.0/23 with gateway 10.20.8.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

rationales.condition: segmentation by function with explicit trunk policy
rationales.rationale: VLAN 30 (Corporate) carries City office users on 10.20.10.0/24 with gateway 10.20.10.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

rationales.condition: segmentation by function with explicit trunk policy
rationales.rationale: VLAN 40 (Management) carries Infrastructure management on 10.20.11.0/25 with gateway 10.20.11.1. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: root (priority 4096).

rationales.condition: segmentation by function with explicit trunk policy
rationales.rationale: VLAN 50 (Guest) carries Visitor access on 10.20.11.128/27 with gateway 10.20.11.129. Trunks permit only VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 999; native VLAN 999 is reserved and unused to prevent double-tagged VLAN hopping. RSTP role: designated.

rationales.condition: loop prevention with deterministic root selection
rationales.rationale: Selected Rapid PVST+ with per-VLAN root priority 4096 on the management VLAN so that each VLAN has a deterministic root and sub-second reconvergence after a topology change.
Selected dual-homed design with a paired gateway peer because the scenario requests resilience beyond a single uplink. HSRP/VRRP removes the gateway as a single point of failure.

rationales.choice: EF priority queue + CS3 signalling bandwidth
rationales.rationale: Selected a strict priority queue for DSCP EF and a reserved bandwidth class for CS3 because the scenario requires 150 ms application latency. Lower latency-sensitive traffic is shaped by class-default.

rationales.condition: traffic crosses an untrusted public WAN
rationales.rationale: Selected an IPsec VPN overlay because the WAN crosses public infrastructure. AES-256/SHA-256 provides confidentiality and integrity, and the tunnel policy limits interesting traffic to the enterprise/cloud prefixes.

configs.switches.cfg:
! NetArchitect generated switch configuration
! Profile: global-wan
! Review interface names, port counts, and PoE budgets before applying.
!
hostname global-wan-sw1
!
ip routing
!
! --- VLAN database ---
vlan 10
 name IOT
!
vlan 20
 name SCANNERS
!
vlan 30
 name CORPORATE
!
vlan 40
 name MANAGEMENT
!
vlan 50
 name GUEST
!
vlan 999
 name NATIVE_UNUSED
!
! --- Spanning tree ---
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
spanning-tree vlan 40 priority 4096
!
! Resiliency: dual-homed. Deploy paired distribution switches and an HSRP/VRRP gateway peer.
!
! --- VLAN gateways (SVIs) ---
interface Vlan10
 description IoT gateway
 ip address 10.20.0.1 255.255.248.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan20
 description Scanners gateway
 ip address 10.20.8.1 255.255.254.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan30
 description Corporate gateway
 ip address 10.20.10.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan40
 description Management gateway
 ip address 10.20.11.1 255.255.255.128
 no shutdown
!
interface Vlan50
 description Guest gateway
 ip address 10.20.11.129 255.255.255.224
 ip access-group GUEST_ISOLATION in
 no shutdown
!
! --- Uplink trunk (explicit allowed VLANs) ---
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description Uplink trunk to distribution/core
 switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk native vlan 999
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30,40,50,999
 switchport nonegotiate
 no shutdown
!
! --- Access ports (sample; expand to match endpoint count) ---
interface GigabitEthernet1/0/1
 description Access - IoT
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 spanning-tree portfast
 spanning-tree bpduguard enable

configs.router.cfg:
! NetArchitect generated router configuration
! Profile: global-wan
!
hostname global-wan-rtr
!
! --- LAN trunk and VLAN subinterfaces ---
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 description LAN trunk to L3 switch
 no ip address
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 description IoT gateway
 encapsulation dot1Q 10
 ip address 10.20.0.1 255.255.248.0
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
 description Scanners gateway
 encapsulation dot1Q 20
 ip address 10.20.8.1 255.255.254.0
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 description Corporate gateway
 encapsulation dot1Q 30
 ip address 10.20.10.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.40
 description Management gateway
 encapsulation dot1Q 40
 ip address 10.20.11.1 255.255.255.128
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.50
 description Guest gateway
 encapsulation dot1Q 50
 ip address 10.20.11.129 255.255.255.224
 no shutdown
!
! --- WAN uplink ---
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 description WAN (ISP Carrier Ethernet + IPsec VPN, N/A (service handoff))
 ip address dhcp
 no shutdown
!
! Default route points at the ISP handoff (replace with real next hop).
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 192.0.2.1
!
! --- OSPF ---
router ospf 1
 router-id 10.20.0.1
 passive-interface default
 no passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 no passive-interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 network 10.20.0.0 0.0.7.255 area 0
 network 10.20.8.0 0.0.1.255 area 0
 network 10.20.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 10
 network 10.20.11.0 0.0.0.127 area 10
 network 10.20.11.128 0.0.0.31 area 20
!
! --- eBGP to cloud VPC (placeholder ASN/peer) ---
router bgp 65000
 bgp router-id 10.20.0.1
 bgp log-neighbor-changes
 neighbor 192.0.2.2 remote-as 64512
 !
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.20.0.0 mask 255.255.248.0
  network 10.20.8.0 mask 255.255.254.0
  network 10.20.10.0 mask 255.255.255.0
  network 10.20.11.0 mask 255.255.255.128
  network 10.20.11.128 mask 255.255.255.224
  neighbor 192.0.2.2 activate
  neighbor 192.0.2.2 route-map FROM-CLOUD in
 exit-address-family
!
route-map FROM-CLOUD permit 10
 set local-preference 200
!
end
configs.acl.cfg:
! NetArchitect generated guest isolation ACL
! Applied inbound on guest SVIs (see switches.cfg).
ip access-list extended GUEST_ISOLATION
 remark Block guest VLANs from internal address space
 deny ip any 10.20.0.0 0.0.255.255
 deny ip any 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255
 deny ip any 172.16.0.0 0.15.255.255
 deny ip any 192.168.0.0 0.0.255.255
 permit udp any any eq 53
 permit tcp any any eq 443
 permit ip any any
!
end
configs.qos.cfg:
! NetArchitect generated WAN QoS policy
! Target application latency: 150 ms
! Apply after router.cfg; the interface already exists there.
class-map match-any VOICE
 match dscp ef
class-map match-any SIGNALLING
 match dscp cs3
!
policy-map WAN-QOS
 class VOICE
  priority percent 30
 class SIGNALLING
  bandwidth percent 10
 class class-default
  fair-queue
  random-detect
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 service-policy output WAN-QOS
!
end
configs.vpn.cfg:
! NetArchitect generated IPsec VPN skeleton
! Replace peer addresses and ASNs with the contracted values.
! Never commit the pre-shared key; configure it out-of-band.
crypto isakmp policy 10
 encr aes 256
 hash sha256
 authentication pre-share
 group 14
 lifetime 28800
!
crypto ipsec transform-set NETARCH-TS esp-aes 256 esp-sha256-hmac
 mode tunnel
!
ip access-list extended VPN-INTERESTING
 permit ip 10.20.0.0 0.0.255.255 172.31.0.0 0.0.255.255
!
crypto map NETARCH-MAP 10 ipsec-isakmp
 set peer 198.51.100.2
 set transform-set NETARCH-TS
 match address VPN-INTERESTING
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 crypto map NETARCH-MAP
!
end
